scenes.text: Most startups don't die from competition. They die from building something nobody wants.
The number one killer is no product-market fit — no real demand for what you made.
Founders fall in love with their idea, not with the customer's actual problem.
Talk to twenty real users before you write a single line of code.
Charge money early. Paying customers are the only proof that matters.
Build what people already pay for — then pour fuel on it.
